I recommend a three-phase 24‑week plan with strict budget caps and gating, executed fully within our governance and pricing policies: Phase 1 (Weeks 1–8) — run a low‑risk pilot in one target segment using a standardized packaged offer (no custom discounts), enact two CX quick wins (top‑3 support fixes), and a focused 2–4 week onboarding/support training; success metrics: conversion, CAC, onboarding time, and NPS delta.  
Phase 2 (Weeks 9–16) — scale the pilot to up to three segments only if gates pass (CAC and conversion targets met and NPS stable/improving); operations implements schedule and workflow shifts, HR runs targeted recruiting for up to two critical roles, and product/sales deploy standardized expansion offers (compliant with pricing rules) while monitoring gross margin weekly.  
Phase 3 (Weeks 17–24) — prioritize retention and expansion by activating account expansion motions for new cohorts, automating the top support pain points to lift CSAT, and running executive‑led customer outreach; acquisition spend is adjusted based on margin and operational capacity.  
At each phase end the CEO/CFO/COO convene a decision gate (go/modify/kill) using five KPIs — new ARR by segment, CAC and payback, expansion ARR, operating margin delta, and NPS/CSAT — with authority to stop scaling to protect margins or operations.  
This sequence accelerates targeted acquisition via test‑and‑scale, grows expansion through standardized add‑ons and account plays, protects margin via caps and weekly monitoring, and raises satisfaction through CX fixes and training — trade‑off: limited early experiment costs may compress margin briefly but are constrained by caps and hard gates to safeguard Q2.
